summary: Two request flood events were flagged against host-01 from ip-01 to ip-02, associated with user-01, occurring between 13:24 and 13:30 UTC.

sequence.description: A request flood was detected against host-01 from ip-01 to ip-02 while user-01 was logged on.
A second request flood was detected against host-01 from ip-01 to ip-02.

findings.statement: Repeated request floods from the same source IP (ip-01) to the same destination IP (ip-02) targeting host-01 suggest a sustained DoS attempt.

impact: host-01 was subjected to two request flood events, which may have degraded its availability or performance.
recommendations: Investigate the source IP ip-01 to determine if it is a known malicious actor or a compromised internal host. Why: Both flagged events originate from ip-01, making it the primary source of the DoS traffic. Less disruptive option: Temporarily rate-limit traffic from ip-01 to host-01 to mitigate impact while investigation proceeds.

Verify the status of user-01 and their session on host-01 to rule out insider threat or compromised credentials. Why: The events are associated with user-01 being logged on, which could indicate the user is the source or a victim of the attack. Less disruptive option: Force a password reset for user-01 and monitor their subsequent activity.
risk_justification: The risk score of 57 (medium) is justified by the presence of two distinct DoS flood events targeting the same host, indicating a persistent threat that could impact service availability.
uncertainty: It is unclear whether user-01 is the attacker, a victim, or simply present during the attack. (would be settled by: Detailed authentication logs, session logs, and user activity logs for user-01 on host-01 and host-02.) The exact volume and duration of the request floods are not specified. (would be settled by: Network traffic logs with packet counts, bandwidth usage, and precise start/end times for each flood event.) The relationship between host-02 and the DoS attack on host-01 is unknown. (would be settled by: Network topology diagrams and logs showing traffic flow between host-01, host-02, ip-01, and ip-02.) Limitations: The analysis is based solely on the provided evidence package and does not include real-time network monitoring or host-level forensic data. The context event (fx-024) on host-02 is not directly linked to the DoS events on host-01, limiting the ability to draw conclusions about cross-host impact.
